claims.text: A hybrid TOR-TILD and machine-learning interatomic-potential approach can improve thermodynamic-property determination for multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperatures.
The target system is a multicomponent high-entropy material in a solid or fluid state near its solid-to-fluid transition.
The intervention combines TOR-TILD with machine-learning interatomic potentials.
The interatomic potentials would be informed by both TOR-TILD and machine-learning algorithms.
High-entropy alloys have a vast compositional design space.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can efficiently sample the compositional space of high-entropy materials.
TOR-TILD provides accurate values for the critical thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy materials near the transition.
The hybrid method can treat both the solid and dense-fluid phases around the transition.
The hybrid method retains ab initio-level accuracy.

The hybrid method will improve the accuracy of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat-capacity predictions relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The hybrid method will improve computational efficiency for determining those transition properties relative to existing methods.
DFT free-energy studies and TOR-TILD results for elemental and binary systems provide appropriate baselines for evaluating the multicomponent method.
The approach is applicable only at compositions and temperatures for which it can be trained and validated.
Transferability of machine-learning interatomic potentials across diverse high-entropy-material compositions is uncertain.
TOR-TILD calculations may incur errors for complex multicomponent systems.
